analysis:
The supplied change to docs/developer/build.md is documentation-only. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and rewrites the CI workflow table and the opt-in PR CI description around lines 358-396 on the head side. It adds opt-in labels (run-ci, run-gpu-ci, run-threat-model), replaces the hourly dev dispatch with manual workflow_dispatch, and describes route retries and watchdog behavior. No provider runtime code, keys, attestation, authorization, cache storage or WebSocket handling changes in the supplied evidence, so I found no regression against the TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011 or T-041 controls.

CI-related security statements in the docs (examined, not verified against the workflows): caches are saved only on master/dev pushes; the Darkbloom cache gate (CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off) keeps GitHub's Actions cache out of Darkbloom runners; the .git restore hook/config sanitization; persist-credentials false; routing falls back on error; the watchdog is limited to actions:write and checks:write; release and signing runs keep literal Blacksmith labels. The workflow YAML, scripts and the full patch are not supplied, so whether the described behavior is implemented, and whether the removal of the hourly dev workflow (ci-dev-hourly.yml) has side effects, is unverified. This is a documentation accuracy question, not a demonstrated vulnerability. T-041 (prefix-cache SSD tier) is unaffected by this text.

Open integration questions: confirm the workflow files match the doc claims, especially cache gating, master strict-cache restore, and that Release Integrity still runs on master PRs.
